merge.title: Wipe as a verified, resumable transaction with a designed post-wipe recovery path (honest verdicts, boot-time 'wipe verified' assertion, complete object list, and an E120/UserID generation-or-reset rule folded into the S-1 ceremony)
merge.threat: Two coupled failures of the 10-wrong-PIN / tamper / admin wipe. (1) Unverified wipe: every caller discards the wipe result and unconditionally prints WALLET WIPED and resets page 124; 'unknown' SE answers are coerced to 'gone'; a failed BHK-derived admin-PIN derivation returns Ok(()) with user objects surviving; the page-125 flag is cleared on the SE050 leg alone, so an OPTIGA-leg failure has no resume; the SE050 sweep omits the duress objects. A power cut, I2C fault or glitch mid-wipe yields a device that claims to be wiped and is not. (2) No recovery after a wipe: on the candidate ship profile (optiga-lock-operational + optiga-hw-counter) E120 is never reset, so every later boot's directional reconcile sees E120_used > page124_used and wipes again; independently the SE050 USERID_OBJ is non-admin-deletable post-S-6 and provisioning hard-refuses when it exists, then panics. 'Restore from seed' is undeliverable and 10 USB PIN attempts turn the hardware, not just the wallet, into a brick (cheap DoS). No runtime OID-range bump exists although three code comments rely on one.
merge.proposal:
ONE work item in two tiers.

TIER A — firmware, landable now (no irreversible SE step):
A1. Honest verdict. `trigger_lockout_wipe` (cmd_request_unlock.rs:190-211), the boot resume (main.rs:1938-1951), the reconcile wipe (nsc/mod.rs:1712-1714) and the provisioning rollback (crypto.rs:495) must consume the `factory_reset_admin` result through a Hamming-distant sentinel (`fi::check_true_into_sentinel`, fail-in = not wiped). Only on a verified result: clear the wipe flag, reset page 124, show WALLET WIPED. Otherwise show 'WIPE INCOMPLETE - reboot to resume', keep the flag armed, keep page 124 charged.
A2. Tri-state readback, never coerce. SE050 already has a post-wipe existence loop (se050/mod.rs:2415-2460) but uses `check_exists(..).unwrap_or(false)` (transport error = 'gone'); make it Absent/Present/Unknown with Unknown = not wiped. Add the missing OPTIGA leg: shielded read-back that F1D1/F1D2/F1D3/F1D4 (+F1D8..F1DB under duress-pin) are blank and F1E1 == RESET_SENTINEL. Remove the `se050_admin_pin()` failure path that returns `Ok(())` after an unauthenticated sweep (se050/mod.rs:3193-3205) - it must return Err.
A3. Flag ownership. The page-125 flag is cleared only by the dual-SE layer after BOTH legs verify (today SE050's `erase_admin_page` at se050/mod.rs:3222-3224 clears it even if `reset_optiga_for_admin` failed, dual_se.rs:631-640). Bound the resume: after N failed boot resumes show a terminal 'WIPE INCOMPLETE - SE fault' screen rather than spinning.
A4. Boot-time 'wipe verified' assertion: when the flag is clear, page 124 blank and the wizard is about to run, re-run the A2 readback; any surviving data object re-arms the wipe (Ledger 1.4 shape).
A5. Completeness: add DURESS_ENTROPY/VK/BOOTSTRAP_VK (0x7B10_0011..13) to DATA_AND_CANARY_OBJS and DURESS_USERID (0x7B10_0010) to the best-effort list; fix the comment at se050/mod.rs:66-71 that claims they are reclaimed. Fold #129 legacy OIDs into the same list review.
A6. Order: keep 'arm flag first'; within the wipe do the SE050 UserID-gated data deletes first (single SCP03 session, admin-deletable, verified by existence), then OPTIGA blank-writes, then MCU pages. Do NOT touch page 126/BHK (see dropped parts).
A7. Tests: commit and wire the untracked `secure/src/secure_lockout_wipe_fi_pure_tests.rs` (WipeFault hooks in MockSecureElement) into CI - but put the verdict/flag DECISION logic in a workspace crate, because nsc/hw modules are `#[cfg(not(test))]` and tests inside them never run. Extend `make pin-gate-wipe-e2e` with a COLD reboot after the wipe and assert 'wizard reached, no second wipe, provisioning succeeds, unlock succeeds' (today it re-provisions in-run on a non-locked build and never calls boot-only `reconcile_pin_attempts`, main.rs:3341-3345).
A8. Stop lying on the screen until Tier B lands: on any build where recovery is not implemented, the post-wipe string must not promise 'restore from seed'.

TIER B — ceremony-design input for S-1 (paper + sacrificial part; no metadata lands from this item):
B0. State the invariant explicitly, Trezor-style: 'every path that can reset or retire the attempt counter must destroy a secret the unlock needs; every wipe path must be able to reset or retire the counter'. Reject any S-1 ceremony that does not satisfy both halves.
B1. Pick one of two designs and rehearse it on a sacrificial OPTIGA:
 (a) Trezor indirection: split F1D0's role into a PIN_SECRET-like object (Change=ALW, Read=Auto(stretched-PIN object)) and the HMAC AuthRef whose Change=Auto(PIN_SECRET-like object), with E120 Change tied the same way. Resetting then necessarily overwrites the secret that half_O/master unwrapping depends on, so Change no longer has to be Auto(F1D0) to stop desoldered-chip brute force (this is the same question #5/#12 are trying to answer). Requires half_O to be bound to that secret, not merely access-gated.
 (b) Generations: a monotonic 'credential generation' g selects the OID set {AuthRef, LUC, data} on OPTIGA and {UserID, data} on SE050; wipe retires g and the wizard provisions g+1; reconcile compares page 124 only against the LUC of the CURRENT generation. SE050 has ample OID space; OPTIGA does not - only four counters E120..E123 exist and E121 is taken by the duress LUC, so (b) alone gives at most ~2-3 lifetime wipes unless combined with (a) or unless duress shares a LUC. g must be derivable from SE state (first generation whose UserID/AuthRef is absent) or stored redundantly, and rolling g back must only ever reach a verified-empty, locked generation.
B2. Resolve the SE050 orphan in the same design: either provision under a fresh UserID OID per generation, or give USERID_OBJ a delete policy that is only satisfiable after the data objects it gates are gone (re-opening S-6 needs its own review). Remove or redesign the hard refusal + panic at se050/mod.rs:1993-2001 / crypto.rs:472-496 accordingly.
B3. Until B1/B2 are chosen, reconcile on the locked profile must not treat 'E120 of an already-wiped wallet > fresh page 124' as tamper: gate the comparison on `is_provisioned()` (F1E1 sentinel) so a wiped device reaches the wizard instead of re-wiping every boot.

members.note: Backbone of Tier A. Kept: honest verdict, boot-time re-assertion, duress OIDs in the SE050 sweep, restoring the untracked FI matrix. Its cited OPTIGA readback 'GetDataObject must fail' is wrong for this design (objects are blank-written, not deleted) - changed to 'reads blank / sentinel'. 'Destroy-fastest-first' kept only as SE050-then-OPTIGA ordering. Priority lowered from P0: duress-pin is not in PROD_SHIP_FEATURES.

Kept: sentinel/double-read verdicts with unknown = not wiped, boot assertion that holds the flag until both SEs and the MCU pages are confirmed, duress set in the wipe list. Dropped: BHK-first regeneration (self-inflicted permanent SE050 lockout on pq1, conflicts with #204/#712 and the re-opened BHK-axis decision) and the journal 'wiped at boot N' receipt (new durable state on page 127, which is owned by the first-boot journal; low value). Its claim that the flag 'covers only the SE050 admin object' is imprecise: the flag is shared and armed by both legs (optiga/mod.rs:2779-2782, se050/mod.rs:3209) but CLEARED by the SE050 leg only.

Kept as Tier B, reframed as ceremony-design input per the deferral decision. Mechanism verified in code (see live_defects) but two corrections: (1) it is a wipe-on-every-boot, not a blocking loop - reconcile returns and boot proceeds to the wizard, where the SEPARATE and already-tracked F23 mechanism (SE050 USERID orphan -> provisioning refusal -> panic) is what actually parks the device; (2) 'saturated to 10' is the display clamp - E120's limit is 32 and the value is whatever the OPTIGA counted. Design (b) gains a hard constraint the member missed: only four OPTIGA counters exist (E120..E123), E121 already used. The BitBox02 Nova precedent is taken from the member's citation and not re-verified here.

dropped_parts: SE-07 (1) BHK-first: regenerate page-126 BHK before touching the SEs. On pq1 the final SE050 SCP03 and admin-PIN are derived from BHK (se050/mod.rs:3170-3185), so killing BHK first makes the subsequent SE050 delete AND any later re-provision impossible: half_E stays on the chip unverifiably and the device is a guaranteed brick - exactly the #204 ship-gate / #712 hazard. Trezor's secret_safety_erase precedent does not transfer: there BHK wraps flash storage, not the SE pairing credentials. Also collides with the BHK-axis decision re-opened 2026-09-21.
SE-07 (5) journal receipt 'wiped at boot N': adds durable state to page 127 (owned by the first-boot journal) for forensic value only; no security property.

SE-07 (3) 'pages 123-127 blank' as the boot assertion: page 126 (wrapped BHK) and page 127 (journal + PBS salt) must NOT be blank after a wipe or both SE tunnels are lost; page 123 counter policy across a wipe is a separate invariant-#9 question. Assertion narrowed to page 124 + flag + SE objects.

pin-02 (2) OPTIGA readback phrased as 'GetDataObject must fail' and SE-07's 'F1E1/F1D1 absent via check_exists': OPTIGA objects are blank-written, never deleted; correct check is blank contents + F1E1 == RESET_SENTINEL.
pin-02 (2) 'add SE050 post-wipe readback': already implemented for the data/canary list (se050/mod.rs:2415-2460); only the coercion and the list are wrong.
pin-01 'permanent boot-wipe LOOP' wording: refuted as stated - reconcile wipes and returns (nsc/mod.rs:1712-1716); the parking mechanism is F23's panic. Kept as 'wipes every boot + unprovisionable'.

pin-01 design (a) as literally written (a separate wipe-only AuthRef gated by its own LUC and derived from DHUK/BHK): a DHUK-derived credential is recomputable by any secure-world image (round-1 fact d) and consumes one of the two remaining counters; replaced by the Trezor PIN_SECRET indirection, which needs no new secret.
Any landing of OPTIGA metadata or LcsO change from this item: S-1/S-2/S-3 are deferred by design; Tier B is paper + sacrificial-part rehearsal only.

No runtime OID-range bump exists to escape.

merge.residual_after: Tier A only: the wipe is honest and resumable but the device is still unrecoverable after a wipe on the locked profile, so anyone with 10 PIN attempts (USB or buttons) still destroys the hardware; a persistent SE fault now yields a permanent 'WIPE INCOMPLETE' device instead of a false 'WIPED' one (a visible oracle that one SE survived - acceptable given the XOR split). An attacker who can cut power or glitch still delays the wipe indefinitely by never letting a boot complete; the surviving half stays behind its SE's own silicon counter (SE050 UserID max-10, E120 limit 32), which is the real bound, not the MCU. Readback goes through the same I2C tunnels, so an interposer that holds the tunnel keys could fake 'absent' - only if DHUK/BHK-derived SCP03/PBS keys are already compromised. A wipe cannot be acted on while unpowered (no battery; tamper is handled at next boot). With Tier B: lockout becomes a wallet-wipe DoS rather than a hardware brick, still a cheap DoS against a user without their mnemonic to hand; design (b) is bounded by OPTIGA's four counters, after which the device is a brick again; design (a) rests on unvalidated OPTIGA access-condition behaviour until rehearsed on silicon; generation-index rollback reaches only empty locked generations if A2 verification held at retirement. Nothing here addresses attempts burned with no user error (#692/#715), a forged status word driving a wipe (#104/#120), or desoldered-chip attacks on F1D0 before S-1 closes.

skeptic.reason:
The core holds: every wipe call site discards the verdict, and the locked ship profile has no post-wipe recovery. All six live defects were confirmed by reading the executing code under PROD_SHIP_FEATURES (Makefile:2718); nothing was run on silicon. The advisor call was rate-limited, so this pass has no second-reviewer check.

The recommendation is not refuted, but it needs six corrections before anyone acts on it:
- **A2's OPTIGA readback cannot be built as written.** The data objects are not readable without PIN auth, so "reads blank" is unverifiable after a lockout.
- **The flag bug is worse than stated.** A transport failure on the SE050 leg clears the wipe flag, and the admin object is deleted even when data deletes failed.
- **There is a third brick mechanism the merge missed.** Under the locked profile, re-provisioning fails at the first OPTIGA write (F1D0), before the SE050 orphan or E120 matter.
- **B3 buys nothing on its own.** It turns "re-wipe every boot" into "reach a wizard that cannot provision".
- **Two "untracked" claims are wrong.** #123 already records the E120 re-wipe and the missing OPTIGA readback.
- **A1 as worded creates a new permanent state.** "Keep page 124 charged" plus a persistent SE fault means wipe-on-every-boot forever; the bounded terminal screen is mandatory, not optional.

P1 is right: the ship profile does not build (S-2 fence) and nothing has shipped. Tier A is still worth landing now because the discarded verdict is feature-independent.
skeptic.corrections:
1. **A2 OPTIGA readback is infeasible as written.** `build_metadata_protected` gives the data OIDs Read = `Auto(F1D0) AND Conf(E140)` for entropy/master and `Auto(F1D0)` for the VKs (secure/src/optiga/apdu.rs:1174-1199; used at optiga/mod.rs:1290, 1330). After a lockout the firmware has no PIN, so it cannot read F1D1..F1D4 to see they are blank. Only F1E1 (Read=ALW) is readable. The OPTIGA verdict must instead be: each blank-write's own status (already propagated with `?`, optiga/mod.rs:2826-2843), plus F1E1 == RESET_SENTINEL, plus optionally a second idempotent blank-write. The same flaw is in #123's "readback-verify every OID". A4's boot assertion is therefore SE050 existence + F1E1 only on the OPTIGA side.

2. **A3 understates the flag bug.** `admin_exists()` returns false on `init()` failure and on a `check_exists` transport error (se050/mod.rs:678-686). So `if !self.admin_exists() { erase_admin_page() }` (se050/mod.rs:3222-3224) clears the resume flag exactly when the SE050 is unreachable. Separately, `admin_factory_reset` self-deletes ADMIN_WIPE_OBJ even when the data-object deletes returned Err (se050/mod.rs:2329-2377). That leaves surviving data objects, no admin authority to delete them later, and a cleared flag. Fix: delete the admin object only after the data objects are verified absent, and make `admin_exists` tri-state.

3. **Missing third brick mechanism.** On the locked profile `provision_auth_ref` starts with `set_data_object(OID_AUTH_REF, pin_secret)` and returns Err on failure (optiga/mod.rs:1123-1131). F1D0 is `Change=Auto(F1D0)` at LcsO=Op and the wipe deliberately skips blanking it for that reason (optiga/mod.rs:2832-2840). So post-wipe OPTIGA provisioning cannot install a new PIN. That is independent of the SE050 USERID orphan and of E120. Tier B must solve three things, not two; design (b) needs a per-generation AuthRef OID on OPTIGA as well.

4. **B3 alone is close to zero value.** Gating reconcile on `is_provisioned()` only swaps "TAMPER DETECT, wipe again" for "wizard, then provisioning failure and panic" (crypto.rs:472-496). It also does not cover the case the recommendation itself names: a re-provisioned wallet with stale E120 is "provisioned" and would still be wiped. Keep B3 only as part of the chosen Tier-B design, not as a standalone interim fix.

5. **Tracking errors in `untracked_delta`.** Item (1), the E120 re-wipe, is already in #123: "stale E120 (never reset on re-provision) → deterministic false-tamper wipe of a healthy restored wallet, saturation → permanent boot-wipe loop". Item (6), no OPTIGA post-wipe readback, is also #123: "No post-wipe readback anywhere". #123 also asks for "blank secrets first, sentinel last", which contradicts the in-code sentinel-first rationale (optiga/mod.rs:2821-2825). The merge is silent on that; it needs a decision. With readback impossible (correction 1), sentinel-last is the safer order, because F1E1 is then the only readable proof that the blank-writes ran. #127 questions whether the boot-reconcile OPTIGA leg runs at all (no `init()` before `ensure_shield`).

6. **A1 creates a new terminal state.** "Keep page 124 charged, keep the flag armed" plus main.rs:1936-1938 (`attempts_exhausted` triggers a wipe) means a persistent SE fault wipes on every boot forever. A3's bounded-resume terminal screen is a hard requirement of A1. It needs a durable resume counter on page 125, which is new per-wipe state that needs review.

7. **Live defect 1 wording.** It is correct by code read but conditional on the shield being up at reconcile time. `pin_attempt_count` returns None if `ensure_shield` fails (optiga/mod.rs:3260-3262, 542-545), and #127 doubts that it succeeds. Mark it "by code read, conditional". The "E120 at 10" figure is the clamp at optiga/mod.rs:3270.

8. **Live defect 2, e2e discrepancy explained in part.** `pin-gate-wipe-e2e` builds with `otp-hardcoded-master-key`, without `optiga-lock-operational` or `bhk` (Makefile:3407-3410; Cargo.toml:457). It is not the ship profile, so its "re-provisions to prove recovery" claim says nothing about ship behaviour. How it gets past the `userid_exists && admin_pin.is_some()` guard (se050/mod.rs:1996-2003) I did not trace.

9. **A7 extra dependency.** The untracked test file depends on `WipeFault` / `inject_wipe_fault` in another session's uncommitted `secure_element.rs` (main.rs:411-420). Committing the test file alone breaks a clean checkout.

10. **Duress severity.** #123 says F1DA holds the decoy master unsplit (dual_se.rs:219), and the OPTIGA duress blanks are `let _ =` (optiga/mod.rs:2862-2866). The "one half is information-free" argument does not cover F1DA. This matters only if duress-pin ships.

11. **A6 ordering.** Today's order is OPTIGA then SE050 (dual_se.rs:631-632). SE050-first is reasonable because SE050 is the leg that can be verified by existence. But on a lockout the SE050 UserID is already silicon-locked, so the ordering gain is small. Do not present it as a security improvement.

skeptic.untracked_delta:
After removing what #123 already covers, the untracked items are:
1. `admin_exists()` coerces a transport or init failure to "gone", which clears the page-125 resume flag when the SE050 is unreachable (se050/mod.rs:678-686, 3222-3224).
2. ADMIN_WIPE_OBJ is self-deleted even when data deletes failed, stranding survivors with no delete authority (se050/mod.rs:2329-2377).
3. `se050_admin_pin()` failure returns Ok(()) (se050/mod.rs:3193-3205).
4. Page 124 is reset and "WALLET WIPED / restore from seed" is shown unconditionally at three call sites; #123 names only the swallowed arm.
5. On the locked profile F1D0 cannot be rewritten after a wipe, so OPTIGA provisioning fails at its first APDU (optiga/mod.rs:1123-1131). This is a third brick mechanism; neither #168 nor #123 states it.
6. OPTIGA data OIDs are not readable without PIN auth, so the "readback-verify" fix requested in #123 and in this recommendation is infeasible. The verdict must rest on write status plus the F1E1 sentinel, which argues for sentinel-last.
7. The "OID-range bump" escape that code comments rely on has no runtime implementation.
8. OPTIGA has four counters total, which bounds a generation scheme.
9. No issue asks for a boot-time wipe-verified assertion.
10. The lockout-wipe FI suite is untracked, depends on an uncommitted `WipeFault` in secure_element.rs, and would not execute inside cfg(not(test)) modules.
11. No issue states the S-1 acceptance invariant: resettable under all circumstances, and reset destroys a needed secret.
12. `pin-gate-wipe-e2e` proves recovery only on a non-locked `otp-hardcoded-master-key` build; its Makefile text reads as if recovery is proven.
decision_conflicts: S-1/S-2/S-3 deferred by design: Tier B must stay paper plus sacrificial part. The recommendation respects this.
S-6 (resolved 2026-05-28): USERID_OBJ has no admin-delete entry on purpose. Any B2 variant that adds a delete policy re-opens S-6; only the per-generation OID variant avoids it.

In-code designed-brick statements (se050/mod.rs:2011-2021 'chip is single-use post-lockout'; optiga/mod.rs:2795-2800) versus the UI string 'restore from seed' and CLAUDE.md's validated wipe flow. This needs an owner ruling; Tier B has no mandate until then. A8 (stop promising restore) is the only part that is unconditionally correct.

Sentinel-first ordering in optiga factory_reset (optiga/mod.rs:2821-2825, deliberate) versus #123's 'blank secrets first, sentinel last'. The recommendation picks neither. With readback infeasible, sentinel-last is the only way F1E1 can attest that the blank-writes ran. Changing it reverses a recorded in-code rationale (a crash mid-wipe must boot as unprovisioned), which the armed flag already covers.

Invariant #2: B3 must not be described as, or turned into, three-way reconciliation. Gating on is_provisioned() also removes rollback detection for a half-wiped device where F1E1 already holds the sentinel but data survives; the flag covers that only if correction 2 is applied.

Bounded-resume counter and any generation index are new durable MCU state. Page 127 belongs to the first-boot journal and page 126 to the wrapped BHK. Page 125 is the only candidate, and its erase is currently coupled to the SE050 leg.

BHK axis (memory feedback_keep_bhk_se050_axis; #204/#712): dropping BHK-first regeneration is correct. Note that live defect 4 (admin-PIN derivation failure) is the same BHK-loss hazard seen from the wipe side. Returning Err there, as A2 requires, makes a BHK-less device permanently 'WIPE INCOMPLETE'; that is honest but terminal.
